post.description:
Adds a location to your program, or updates one already in it.

An `id` updates that location; failing that a known `external_id` does; failing both, the address is matched against locations already known to Ekho and a new one is created only if nothing matches. Sending the same `external_id` again updates rather than conflicts, so a nightly full sync is safe to run.

Neither identifier is required. Omit `external_id` and work off the `id` returned. Renaming an `external_id` means sending `id` alongside the new value.

Adding a location needs `name` and `address`. An update, by `id` or by a known `external_id`, may omit either and keeps what is stored. A `name` on an update sets what your program calls the location and takes effect at checkout. An `address` naming the same building is accepted however it is spelled. One naming a different building moves the location when Ekho created it through this API for your program alone and the new address is in the same state; otherwise it returns 409 for Ekho to review, and nothing is changed.

A new `external_id` whose address matches a location your program already holds under another `external_id` returns 409 rather than taking that location over. Update it by its `id` instead. Prices are never sent or returned, and each service is charged at your program's own rate.

id.description: An Ekho location id. Updates that location, and is required to change its external_id.

external_id.description: Your own id for this location. Unique within your program.

services.description: The services this location performs for your program.

name.description: What your program calls this location. This is the name a buyer sees at checkout. Required to add a location; an update that omits it keeps the current name.

address.description: Required to add a location. An update that omits it keeps the current address. One naming a different building moves the location when Ekho created it through this API for your program alone and the move stays in the same state; otherwise it returns 409 for Ekho to review.

email.description: Business contact, not a person. Every write saves it for your program and reads return it as you sent it; an update that omits it keeps the last value.

phone.description: Business contact, not a person. Every write saves it for your program and reads return it as you sent it; an update that omits it keeps the last value.

201.description: The location was added to your network.

post.description: Replays a recorded event to every destination currently subscribed to its type, plus any legacy subscription on the account. The stored envelope is sent verbatim, so you receive what the original delivery should have sent rather than a re-render of current state. Targets are resolved at replay time, so a destination added or repointed since the original fire receives it. Attempts are recorded against the same event and are distinguishable from the original delivery. Replaying is safe to repeat; treat the delivered event as a duplicate and key off the event `id`.

post.description: Creates a checkout cart for the account bound to the token and returns it with a `checkout_url` the buyer can be sent to. The account that owns the cart is resolved server-side from the token, so the request carries no owner identifiers. Buyer prefill is optional. The cart holds one dealer unit, named by `inventory_id`. The body takes no vehicle list, no accessory field, and no preorder flag, because a unit is a specific vehicle that already exists rather than a configuration to build. To sell a vehicle to be built instead, use `POST /carts/build-to-order`.
